checks.run: cd app && pnpm exec svelte-kit sync && pnpm exec svelte-check --threshold error && pnpm test -- --run
checks.why: The frontend half of `just check` and `just test`. The setup step is not optional and not a convenience: this repo keeps its real lockfile in app/, while the root pnpm-lock.yaml has a single empty importer, so `pnpm install` at the root reports 'Already up to date' and installs nothing at all. CI gets this right by running its install step with working-directory: app; a local run that skips it fails svelte-check with four 'Cannot find name process / node:fs' errors that look like a tsconfig defect and are actually an empty node_modules

checks.run: cargo check --workspace && cd app/src-tauri && cargo check
checks.why: Mirrors check-linux, the one Rust job left on the PR path, plus the workspace check from check-macos. KNOWN TO FAIL ON THIS BOX, and the cause is upstream rather than this manifest: llama-cpp-sys-2 0.1.146's build.rs runs cmake --target install into a prefix it does not own and panics at build.rs:1110 with Os { code: 17, AlreadyExists } the moment that prefix is already populated. Once one build wedges that way, every later cargo invocation reusing the same build directory fails identically in about a minute, which reads like a code error and is not one. Reproduced four times, including from a clean target/ and with --all-targets dropped. To unwedge: rm -rf target/debug/build/llama-cpp-sys-2-* and cargo clean -p llama-cpp-sys-2. Nothing is left unverified by this: check-linux still runs cargo check on the shipped app on every PR, and check-macos runs the full lint/check/test on every push to main. serial+lock:cargo-build because a full workspace build is memory-hungry on this shared box, so it queues behind another checkout's cargo build rather than piling onto it

KNOWN TO FAIL ON THIS BOX for the same upstream reason as rust-check, see that check's note for the diagnosis and the unwedge recipe. Left here rather than deleted because the check itself is right: check-macos runs it for real on every push to main, so this is a local gap and not a verification hole
